record_notes.DCP-LETT-1442: July 17 with supplied 1851 year. Explicitly thanks Huxley note of July 10 and echinoderm report, the latter read with interest and used for conceptual distinction between individuals and zooids. Agreement on distinction coexists with doubt ordinary terminology will change. Incoming cover not preserved; reported content and published report do not manufacture a surviving letter prompt. Later historical scholarship remains apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1457: October 9, 1851 explicitly written. Individual Darwin testimonial based on Huxley publications and voyage studies; current application success only wished. Toronto identification and eventual unsuccessful outcome from apparatus, not yet outcome known in letter. Missing solicitation, other scientists separate testimonials not Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1462: November 22 with supplied 1851 year. Asks Ray Society membership before offering volume, address unknown so routes through Taylor. Not a dispatch or receipt proof. Edition dated 1851 but apparatus says copies unavailable for distribution until late January 1852; later presentation list cannot backdate delivery to November. No surviving response to membership query.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1514: April 11 with supplied 1853 year established from year-since-publication reference, not 1852 catalogue order. Carrier is copy plus incomplete autograph, not unqualified complete ALS; all five surviving body blocks read. Ascidia offer follows oral remark, specimens still to be removed from bottles, old notes called inadequate. Müller 1852 reprint possessed and offered, no full-reading claim and no identified covering letter. Huxley review intention oral; publication requested and speculative, not a completed review. Later 1856/1857 notice and criticism, and modern reidentification of Beagle specimens are apparatus, not current feedback.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1480: April 23 with supplied 1853 year, later than 1514 despite lower ID. Specimens taken out but unexamined condition; bottle to Gray next Thursday, not delivery already completed. Encloses habitat catalogue and copied observations, not fully reproduced in this preserved letter body or scholarly siblings; missing enclosure stays missing. Mollusc paper explicitly read all; Huxley abstract archetype accepted differently from Owen/Agassiz usage, anamorphism disagreement retained. Cleodora variability prediction is hypothesis and request for evidence. Cementing-from-ovarian-content claim dated Darwin interpretation, with Milne-Edwards disbelief recalled from earlier oral meeting; later correction of Proteolepas taxonomy and Huxley 1857 lecture not current.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1587: September 2 with supplied 1854 year. Second volume now published, Huxley copy to be sent next Thursday. Six obligated recipients listed, possible additional names queried, Royal Society shipping only a question. Later presentation-list changes are not yet decisions. Has read Huxley Vestiges review and endorses much while considering it harsh; distinguishes own species unorthodoxy from unphilosophical argument and treats Agassiz embryological evidence as weak but hoped true. Later Huxley 1887 regret and Origin citation are not present knowledge. No preserved incoming note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1590: September 8 with supplied 1854 year. Thanks missing Huxley note; asks which of two Leuckarts and encloses distribution list absent here. Own book sent to Jermyn Street, Baily reports forwarding to Lankester; no direct evidence of Huxley final receipt. Agrees branchiae derive from ovigerous fraena, reflects on beginner dissection and shares Owen/science view. P8 Leydig address/publication uncertain, Krohn route tentative; P9 follows Williams and Norgate advice. This is not Vestiges/Agassiz discussion from 1587, nor a request for anatomical clarification as revision 1 incorrectly said. Friedrich Sigismund death is editorial identification, not explicit current Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1592: September 13 with supplied 1854 year. Two missing Huxley notes acknowledged. Has sent copies to Koelliker instead of hard-to-reach Leydig and to Vogt, exhausting his own stock. Proposes future examination of named Balanus structures; instructions are historical source content. P5 Huxley has duplicate book, with Ray membership supplied by apparatus, distinct from previous forwarding report. Later 1857 tentative support and disagreements do not become 1854 reply content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1635: February 20 with supplied 1855 year. Sends cirripede preparations and moulding specimen to test whether suspected structures are foreign organisms; asks future corroboration. Prior Brachiopod anus observation read some time ago is distinct from new Mollusca article received this morning and not yet read. Parcel route through Percy does not establish arrival. P6 is Darwin authorial specimen memorandum with identifiers 280, 219, 203, 285, 179 and return request, not editorial apparatus. Raw MathML gives one-quarter followed by th for focal distance; flattened 14th cannot be read as fourteen. No unit inferred beyond source. Complete enclosure as preserved in body read.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1645: March 8 with supplied 1855 year. Missing Huxley report has examined preparations; Darwin thankful yet maintains own ovarian/cement interpretation and admits weak microscopic knowledge. Separates firm anatomical assertions from uncertain germinal-vesicle idea. Explains larval analogy-based classification, Dana agreement versus limb-homology disagreement and Milne-Edwards difference. Unidentified paper about parasite mistaken for ovarium had been stopped; source not invented. P8 now explicitly read Mollusca article with attention, later than February 20 physical receipt/unread stage. Own opinion limited by ignorance, requests better lectures for learners; no later correction silently inserted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1659: March 31 with supplied 1855 year. Royal Society medal planning, not a zoological observation question. Wishes to nominate Westwood but asks Huxley to critique enclosed remarks and seeks seconder. Enclosed draft citation absent; later final printed citation cannot replace its exact wording. Entire Westwood Classification read before Council and considering medal; September 1854 reading date supplied by separate notebook apparatus. Hancock comparison and possible Lyell Copley claim undecided; later November awards, Bell seconding and Lyell 1858 award remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1668: April 18 with supplied 1855 year. Forwards missing Bell opinion, asks recipient to read and burn: historical quoted instruction does not authorize any file deletion. Acknowledges Lindley higher claim but uncertain about alternating biological subfields; weighs Hancock/Westwood and quotes Huxley opinion to Bell. Has written Bell but meeting and final award decisions still future. Huxley note on Lyell separate missing input. Reports De la Beche death. Later rule history and medal outcomes are editorial evidence, not assumptions about current settled procedure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1759: Day 3 with September 1855 supplied from related drawing chronology. Huxley drawings received and annotated; no separate surviving cover-note text. Actual two preserved images viewed: stalked Lepas anatomy with cement-gland arrow, ovarian branching, oesophagus/stomach and peduncle-muscle directions; sessile Balanus drawing with pencil cross and sub-oesophageal-ganglion placement direction. These combine Huxley imagery and Darwin corrections; cannot use amended image as pristine incoming prompt or turn editorially typeset image captions into invented original prose. Body distinguishes unseen Lepas cement gland from probable position by analogy, and asks ganglion, stomach, antenna and testes changes. No proof original physical ink/pencil layers can be isolated from these reproductions. Later printed revised drawings in 1857 remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1697: Explicit accepted batch-15 primary full reading reused with matching source pins. June 10 with supplied 1855 year. Independently read additional witness in full. Asks Huxley to speak for Barrande and Dana at next council if Darwin cannot attend, explicitly enclosing an old Lyell note; footnote identifies April 23 source 1672 and shared dual candidature plus Barrande primordial work confirms it. Conditional request not to answer if attending does not prove attendance. Huxley lecture abstract has been read with disappointment; exact title identity is apparatus and missing cover note remains missing. Upcoming marriage congratulations are not proof wedding already occurred. Later June 14 and July 21 events separate. This source is not a reply to Lyell but uses his incoming evidence.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed actual stalked cirripede section: appendages and elongated peduncle, left cement-gland arrow/cross near top of peduncle; typeset directions on branching ovarian tubes/caeca, oesophagus bell shape/stomach breadth and transverse/oblique peduncle muscles. Source reproduction mixes drawing, marks and editorially typeset annotation, not pure incoming diagram.

Viewed actual sessile cirripede cutaway: concentric shell/body boundaries, appendages and internal looping structures. Cross near central-right loop accompanies typeset instruction to move main sub-oesophageal ganglion left. No unannotated precursor image can be recovered from this reproduction.

reading_method: Thirteen targets independently read fully, including original XML attributes, copy/incomplete carrier, enclosures present or missing, all footnotes/bibliographies, original 1635 MathML and both actual 1759 figure assets. 1697 reuses prior accepted full primary source reading. Worker original and two revisions preserved; primary source-specific summaries and corrections override faulty first passes.
